desc:
An encoding of a string is a sequence of pieces, where a piece is either a single lowercase letter or k[E] with an integer k ≥ 2 (written in decimal without leading zeros) followed by a non-empty encoding E in square brackets; k[E] stands for the decoding of E repeated k times. Pieces can be nested. The length of an encoding is the number of characters it is written with, counting digits and brackets.

Return the length of the shortest encoding that decodes to s. Always possible: s itself (all letters) is an encoding.

Examples: "abababab" becomes 4[ab] (length 5); "aaaaaaaaaabaaaaaaaaaab" becomes 2[10[a]b] (length 9); "abcd" stays as is (length 4).
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters
hints: Encodings are recursive, so think of the best encoding of every substring s[i..j] as a subproblem (interval DP).
A substring's best encoding is either: the substring itself, a concatenation of the best encodings of two parts, or a repetition k[E] where the substring is some block repeated k times.

For the repetition case, find the smallest period p of the substring that divides its length (the first position where the substring re-appears inside sub + sub). If p is smaller than the length, the cost is digits(k) + 2 + best(block) with k = length / p.
editorial: Let f[i][j] be the shortest encoding length of s[i..j]. A single letter costs 1. Otherwise the candidates are (a) the raw length j - i + 1, (b) a split f[i][m] + f[m+1][j] for every m, and (c) a repetition: if the substring equals a block u repeated k ≥ 2 times, then digits(k) + 2 + f[block].

For (c) only the shortest block (the smallest period dividing the length) needs to be tried. A longer block um repeated k' times can only be encoded as k'[...] around an encoding of um, and that costs at least as much as k'm written once around the encoding of u, since digits(k' m) ≤ digits(k') + digits(m) and the extra brackets cost two more. To find the smallest period, search sub inside sub + sub starting from offset 1; the first hit is the period (equal to the length if the substring is not periodic).

Interval DP is O(n<sup>3</sup>) for the splits plus O(n) per interval for the period test, so O(n<sup>3</sup>) overall with n ≤ 120, and O(n<sup>2</sup>) space. Process intervals by increasing length so that every sub-interval is ready.
